- [should-change] Action cards in the 400px inspector: Each card (When rows + Then instruction + generated param form + summary) will run 450–600px tall; three actions is a 1500px+ scroll in a narrow column, and the plain-words summary — the one line the admin actually scans — sits at the bottom of each card. Save issues also have nowhere to land: `SaveIssue` is `{question, messageKey}` and the popover renders a question number + title, which an action issue does not have.
    → Render each action with `shared/CollapsibleSettingsCard`: title "Action N", subtitle = the plain-words summary (`line-clamp-2`), badge = red `TriangleAlert` when that action has an issue, trash icon in the header row beside the chevron. Track `openIndex` in ActionsPanel state; "Add action" sets it to the new card, all others collapsed. Extend `SaveIssue` to a union `{ kind: "question", question, messageKey } | { kind: "action", index, messageKey }`; the popover renders action entries with subtitle "Action {index+1}" and clicking one calls `revealAction(index)` = `setInspectorTarget("actions")` + `setOpenIndex(index)`. `handleSave` runs the action check between `findFirstInvalidQuestion` and `form.handleSubmit`. Keep inspector placement — no dialog or full-canvas mode; the canvas is the title reference the admin reads while building conditions, and Form settings already established outline-row → panel.
- [should-change] Instruction picker and generated forms: "logging (logging) · NOTIFY" is meaningless to a hospital admin. With exactly one registry instruction, an empty Then block + "Add instruction" is a mandatory click to a foregone choice, and the "zero instructions → save issue" rule then fires on every freshly added action.
    → Label = `t(`action_instruction__${slug}`, { defaultValue: humanize(slug) })` with en.json `action_instruction__logging: "Show a message"`; type badge = `t(`action_type__${instruction_type}`)` in plain words (NOTIFY "Notification", TEXT "Text", PERFORMED "Performed", VALIDATE "Check", REDIRECT "Redirect"); never render the slug. When the registry holds exactly one instruction, "Add action" creates the action with that instruction preselected and `context` auto-resolved, so the admin only fills the message. Param labels come from `input_schema.properties[key].title`, hints from `.description`, required marked with the fill renderer's asterisk pattern; empty required → save issue `action_param_required` ("Action {n}: “{title}” is required").
- [should-change] Expression escape hatch: "Switching back is only offered when the text parses" strands an admin who mangled the text in expression mode with no explanation and no exit. Neither backend nor FE validates syntax, so a typo in expression mode saves clean and 500s for every nurse at fill time; and the passive "help line listing variables" asks the admin to type `q_Q_3f2a9b1c` by hand.
    → Always show "Back to builder". If `parseCondition` returns null, clicking it opens an inline Popover confirm — "This expression can't be shown as rules. Replace it with builder rules? The text will be discarded." [Replace → zero rules / `True`] [Keep expression]. Add a pure `lintExpression(expr, linkIds)` in actionExpression.ts (node-tested) producing save issues: unresolved `q_<id>` token → `action_unknown_question_ref` ("Action {n} uses a question that no longer exists"); `/\b(patient|self)\.[A-Za-z]/` outside quotes → `action_expression_attribute` ("Write patient[\"age\"], not patient.age"); unbalanced `()`/`[]`/quotes → `action_expression_syntax`. Replace the help line with clickable chips (question title → inserts `q_<link_id>` at the caret; "Patient › age" → inserts `patient["age"]`). The plain-words summary shows the raw expression in monospace while in expression mode.
- [should-change] Post-submit outcome feedback (fill page): The success toast fires, then the page navigates to `exitTarget`; an action NOTIFY toast at sonner's ~4s default is gone before the nurse has parsed the new page — and a clinical instruction ("Refer to TB clinic") is exactly what must not be missed. Title = slug is also unreadable.
    → `actionOutcomes.ts` returns `{ kind, title, description? }[]`; `FillPageBody.onSuccess(outcomes, redirect?)` does `autosave.finishDraft(); navigate(redirect ?? exitTarget);` THEN fires the outcome toasts so they stack above the success toast (the Toaster lives in App.tsx with `closeButton` and `expand` already on). Title = the instruction label from the picker finding, never the slug; description = `results.message` when it is a string. Durations: NOTIFY/TEXT/VALIDATE `duration: 15000`, PERFORMED `duration: 6000`. More than 3 outcomes → one `toast.message(t("n_actions_ran", { count }), { description: <ul> of the first 5 lines, duration: 15000 })`. REDIRECT keeps the same-origin `/` path guard and still fires the success toast so the nurse knows the submission went through before landing elsewhere.
- [nice-to-have] Discoverability / reverse lookup: An admin editing, retitling or deleting a question has no cue that it drives an action until the save-time "no longer exists" issue; and for location/device/facility questionnaires the Actions row is a dead end that only says "not available".
    → Compute `actionRefsByLinkId: Map<string, number[]>` once per `state.actions` change (same regex token extraction as the fill guard). StudioOutline `rowAdornment` adds `<Zap className="size-3 text-amber-600" />` beside the existing `Split`, tooltip `t("used_by_actions", { list })`; StudioCanvas's chip row adds a "Used by Action 1" `Zap` chip whose click sets `inspectorTarget: "actions"` and opens that card. Hide the Actions outline row for location/device/facility subject types unless `actions.length > 0`, in which case show it with the existing "runs only for patient and encounter questionnaires" notice and no add button.
- [nice-to-have] Link ID editor (expression-mode legibility): After the generator fix, expression-mode variables read `q_Q_3f2a9b1c`; usable via the insert chips, but unreadable for anyone maintaining a custom expression later.
    → Only if expression mode is expected to be used by humans regularly: add a "Link ID" `Input` at the bottom of the Question tab inside a collapsed `CollapsibleSettingsCard` titled `t("link_id")` (key already exists), validated `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` and unique in the tree (inline error + save issue `link_id_invalid`), with `onChange` dispatching through the same remap path as `makeLinkIdReferenceable` so enable_when and action refs follow the rename. Skip otherwise.

It is wrong or materially incomplete in six places that would make the proposed builder emit conditions that 500 at submit: (1) quantity answers are ALWAYS a `{value, coding, unit}` record and valueset-backed choices clean to `{"coding": …}` with NO `value` key, while option-backed choices are plain strings even when options carry a `code` — the existing `answerIsRecord` gets two of these three wrong; (2) children of a repeating group are not top-level `q_` names; (3) `_actions` is `{}` (not a list) when the questionnaire has no actions; (4) `params` is a required dict and `instructions` is optional on the wire; (5) "PatientQuestionnaire has no fields" is only true of the registry — the evaluator's global-field fallback makes `patient["age"]` resolve there anyway

- [must-change] backend contract / ENG-737 branch state: origin/ENG-737 care/emr/api/viewsets/questionnaire/questionnaire.py:182-184 and :231-233 do `if getattr(request_obj, "actions", None): for action in request_obj.actions` — the spec default is pydantic's MISSING sentinel (spec.py:241), which is truthy and not iterable (verified in the container: `bool(MISSING)=True`, iter → TypeError 'Sentinel' object is not iterable). Every create/PUT that omits `actions` therefore 500s on the pushed branch. The running Docker backend mounts /Users/bodhishthomas/code/care (branch bodhi/ENG-737-test-fixtures) which carries an UNCOMMITTED `_submitted_actions()` guard in that file; the brief's 'verified by live probes' ran against that patch, not origin/ENG-737. Probe also showed `actions: null` → 400 (list_type).
    -> Commit and push the `_submitted_actions()` guard (local uncommitted diff to questionnaire.py) to ENG-737 before any FE work lands, and add a backend test for a PUT without `actions`. On the FE, until that ships: send `actions: []` explicitly in both create bodies (manage/QuestionnaireCreatePage.tsx:100 and manage/CloneQuestionnaireDialog.tsx:107) and make `buildUpdateBody` emit `actions: questionnaire.actions ?? []` (never undefined/null — null is a 400 regardless).

- [must-change] condition compile — per-type value shapes (brief lines 39-41; builder/actionVariables.ts:147-170): Verified by echoing cleaned values through `logging` `{{ }}` params: boolean→True/False ('1' also normalises), integer→int, decimal→float, string/text/date/time/dateTime/url→the FE's serialized strings, repeats→list (even one value). BUT: quantity ALWAYS cleans to `{"value": 70.0, "coding": {...}, "unit": {...}}` because the fill inputs attach unit+coding on every write (form/engine/inputs/numericEntry.ts:50-55; fill/submit/serializeValues.ts:47-52; backend utils.py:504-512) — `q_weight > 1` → "'>' not supported between dict and int" 500. Valueset-backed choice: ChoiceInput.tsx:152-159 stores `{value: code.display, coding}` and serializeValues.ts:54-56 sends `{coding}` ONLY, so the backend cleans to `{"coding": {system, code, display}}` with NO `value` key — `q_x["value"]` → KeyError 500 a
    -> Rewrite `answerIsRecord`/`questionVariables`: quantity → ref `q_x.value` (compiles to `q_x["value"]`), number operators; choice with `answer_value_set` → ref `q_x.coding.code` (compiles to `q_x["coding"]["code"]`), `==`/`!=` with a value control that picks a code from the valueset expansion (useValueSetExpansion) or a text input for the code; choice with `answer_option` → bare `q_x` scalar regardless of `option.code`; repeats valueset choice stays unusable ('coded_multi'). Fix brief lines 39-41 to state these three shapes explicitly. Add node tests for each compile.

- [must-change] condition compile — groups (builder/actionVariables.ts:180-206): `build_cleaned_response` (utils.py:540-561) flattens NON-repeating group children to the top level (so `q_<child>` works) but keys a `repeats` group under its own link_id as a list of dicts: probe returned `q_grp = [{"q_inner": "a"}, {"q_inner": "b"}]`; the children never exist as top-level names. `questionVariables` walks into every group and offers repeating-group children → NameError → 500 at submit.
    -> In `questionVariables`, when walking a group with `repeats`, mark every descendant `unusable: "repeating_group"` (i18n hint: 'Answers inside a repeating group cannot be used in actions') and do not offer the group itself (a list of dicts has no canonical comparison). Add a test with a nested repeating group.

- [must-change] link ids — studio defaults and clone (shared/questionTree.ts:111; manage/CloneQuestionnaireDialog.tsx:125): `q_<link_id>` must be a Python identifier; the studio's default link ids and `regenerateQuestionIds`' `freshLinkId` are `Q-xxxxxxxx` (hyphen). Probe: `q_Q-hy == "h"` parses as `q_Q - hy` and 500s with "No context value found for field hy". So every new question is disabled in the Answers picker until renamed, and cloning a questionnaire that has actions (the clone dialog currently drops `actions` entirely — no remap exists yet) would, once remapped, point every condition at hyphenated ids and 500 every submission of the clone.
    -> Change `freshLinkId` (and the studio's new-question link-id generator) to an identifier-safe form, e.g. `Q_${crypto.randomUUID().slice(0,8)}`; expose the old→new map from `regenerateQuestionIds` and run `remapActionLinkIds` in the clone dialog; keep `isIdentifierSafeLinkId` as the picker gate for legacy ids. Add a clone Playwright assertion that a saved action still fires on the copy.

- [must-change] _actions response shape (brief lines 60-64; fill/submit/actionOutcomes.ts): questionnaire.py:334 initialises `action_response = {}` and only replaces it when `questionnaire.actions` is non-empty (:357-375), so `_actions` is `{}` for questionnaires without actions, `[]` when nothing fired, and a list of `{slug, instruction_type, results}` otherwise (all three verified). In the batch it is at `results[i].data._actions` for the entry whose `reference_id` is the questionnaire id; a ≥500 sub-request yields `{reference_id, status_code}` with no `data` and the whole batch returns 500 and rolls back (batch_request.py:51-58, 71-72; batch_requests.py:14-32; verified).
    -> In `actionOutcomes.ts` read `_actions` through an `Array.isArray` guard and type it `ActionOutcome[] | Record<string, never>`; match batch results by `reference_id === questionnaire.id` (composeBatch.ts:249 already sets it) rather than by index; correct brief line 60.

- [must-change] wire-shape normalisation (src/types/questionnaire/actions.ts:17-28; builder/actionValidation.ts:55): `Action.instructions` defaults to `[]` (base.py:40) and the PUT `{"condition":"True"}` without an `instructions` key saved and read back as-is (probe); `Instruction.params` is a REQUIRED dict (base.py:27 — probe: missing → 400 'Field required', string → 400 'valid dictionary'); slugs starting with `i_` → 400 (base.py:30-35); extra keys on actions/instructions are persisted verbatim (probe). The FE types declare `instructions` required and `actionValidation` calls `action.instructions.length`, so a questionnaire saved by another client without the key crashes the studio.
    -> Normalise in the studio `reset` path (and in `buildUpdateBody`): `instructions: a.instructions ?? []`, `params: i.params ?? {}`, `context: i.context ?? "self"`; always emit `params` (at least `{}`). Add `params` to the brief's required-field list (line 19-22).

- [should-change] context graph — PatientQuestionnaire and global fallback (brief lines 42-49; builder/actionVariables.ts:79-145): `ActionFieldRegistry.register` stores every static field in `_global_fields` by bare name (field.py:18) and `render_all_fields` re-emits them (field.py:40-47) — that is the source of the 'duplicates'. The evaluator falls back to the global table when the root has no such static field (evaluator.py:44-45), so on a PATIENT questionnaire `patient["age"]` and `context: "patient"` resolve fine (probe returned age 77), contradicting the brief's implication that patient questionnaires have no context; conversely bare `age` from any root resolves to `QuestionnaireResponse.age` → AttributeError 500 (probe). The FE's graph-based `reachableContextPaths`/`reachableContextValues` (dedupe key context_type+field, edges via target_context_type, dynamic skipped) is correct for what the registry DECLARES an
    -> Keep the graph-based computation; do not depend on the fallback. File a backend follow-up on ENG-737: register `PatientQuestionnairePatientContext` (fields/patient.py) and stop registering static fields as globals (or at least stop rendering them twice). In UI copy say 'No context fields are available for this questionnaire type yet' rather than asserting it as a rule.

- [should-change] instruction context path semantics (brief lines 53-55): `instruction.context` is a DOTTED path resolved in context mode, not expression syntax: base.py:117-120 evaluates it then looks up `context_cache[instruction.context]` verbatim, so `patient["age"]` as a context would KeyError. `self` works only bare (base.py:80-81; `self` cannot be a registered field, field.py:16-17). Leaf-valued contexts are unsafe: `context: "patient"` followed by `context: "patient.age"` in one evaluation crashed with "'PatientContext' object does not support item assignment" (evaluator.py:36-38 and :80-82 write a dict into the cached wrapper; probe). `self` is the raw QuestionnaireResponse, `patient` is a PatientContext wrapper.
    -> Keep 'Applies to' limited to `self` plus typed edge paths (existing `reachableContextPaths` already excludes leaves) and never offer leaf paths; state dotted-path syntax in the brief. Preselect the option whose contextType equals the instruction's declared `context`, else `self` (logging declares Appointment, never reachable).

- [should-change] {{ }} templates (brief lines 50-52; builder/actionExpression.ts:347-349, 509-517): Detection is exact `startswith("{{") and endswith("}}")` on the raw string (base.py:122-126): probe `" {{ q_name }}"` was delivered literally, yet `parseTemplate` trims first (actionExpression.ts:511) so the editor would show a variable chip for a value the backend treats as text. The evaluated value is the raw Python value, not a string (probe: `{"message": true}`, `38.5`, `["rash","cough"]`, a dict), so `message: {{ q_fever }}` yields a useless NOTIFY payload. The brief's 'partial interpolation is not supported' is misleading: f-strings are whitelisted and work (`{{ f"T {q_temp:.1f} {q_fever}" }}` → "T 38.5 True"; arithmetic `{{ q_count + 1 }}` → 4). Only top-level string params are templated (base.py:121-131); nested JSON is not.
    -> Make `parseTemplate` non-trimming (or normalise stray whitespace on save). For string-typed params, have the 'insert variable' control compile the whole field to an f-string `{{ f"…" }}` with Python-literal escaping (`\`→`\\`, `"`→`\"`, `{`→`{{`, `}`→`}}`) and parse that subset back (compileFString/parseFString beside compileTemplate, node-tested); keep bare `{{ ref }}` for non-string params. Note in the brief that templates return typed values and that the JSON textarea is never templated.

- [should-change] fill-side failure UX (fill/submit/useSubmitFillSession.ts:146-171; mapBatchErrors.ts:45-61): Every action-evaluation failure is an unhandled ValueError/ExecutionException (base.py:96-106 re-raises as ValueError; :117-131 does not catch at all) that `emr_exception_handler` (base.py:26-56) does not map, so the direct endpoint returns a 500 and the batch wraps it as `{"detail":"server_error"}` with no `errors` — `mapBatchErrors` then shows the generic 'validation_failed' text and the clinician cannot tell an author bug from their own input. Verified 500 triggers: unanswered/enable_when-hidden `q_` reference (disabled questions are stripped before cleaning, utils.py:615-627 + questionnaire.py:370-374), whitespace-only condition, dict/str comparisons, unknown context path, disallowed nodes in a template, `{{ patient }}` (not JSON-serialisable).
    -> In `useSubmitFillSession.onError`, when any failed result has `status_code >= 500` and its `reference_id` matches a session questionnaire id, toast a dedicated i18n string (e.g. 'This questionnaire's automation failed to run, so nothing was saved. Ask the form's author to check its actions.') instead of the validation fallback; keep the per-question mapping for 400s unchanged.

- [should-change] author-side warnings and save validation (brief lines 130-132, 148-151; builder/actionValidation.ts): The 'unanswered → 500' trap is wider than 'not required': a referenced question hidden by `enable_when` (or inside a disabled group) is removed before cleaning and counts as unanswered; `composeBatch` (fill/submit/composeBatch.ts:148) skips disabled questions on the FE too. Comparison typing errors also 500 (`q_temp > "38"` → 'float and str'; probe) and `q_sevc == "C1"` on a coded answer is silently False. Nothing at save time catches `patient.age` (attribute access), list literals, `is None`, tuples — all rejected by evalidate only at submit (verified).
    -> Extend the soft warning to referenced questions that carry `enable_when` or sit under a group with `enable_when` ('If this question is hidden or left unanswered, the submission fails'). In expression mode add a cheap lint from the existing tokenizer: flag `other` tokens (a `.` outside a number = attribute access, `is`, `[`/`(` followed by a literal = list/tuple literal) as a save issue `action_issue_expression_unsupported`. Builder must type literals from the target shape (unquoted numbers for integer/decimal/quantity/`patient.age`).

- [should-change] fill-side outcome scope (brief 'Fill-side outcomes'): Only `logging` (NOTIFY, echoes its params — base.py:43-49, logging_test.py:22-26) exists; REDIRECT/VALIDATE/TEXT/PERFORMED handling and same-origin redirect navigation have no consumer, which conflicts with the owner's 'no extension points without a second consumer' constraint. `instruction_type` arrives as the enum's string value.
    -> Implement NOTIFY only: if `results.message` is a string, `toast.info(message)`; for any other entry `toast.info(t('action_ran', {slug}))`. Drop the REDIRECT navigation path and the `onSuccess(redirect?)` signature change until a REDIRECT instruction ships.

- [nice-to-have] date/time/url operators (brief line 128): Cleaned values are exactly the strings the FE serialises: date `yyyy-MM-dd` (serializeValues.ts:27-33), time `HH:mm:ss` (:37-46), dateTime ISO with offset (:34-36), url verbatim (probe). Equality on dateTime is practically unusable (offset formatting varies) and string comparison operators are not offered anyway.
    -> Offer `is`/`is not` with a date input for `date` only; hide `time`, `dateTime` and `url` from the builder picker (mark `unusable: "type"` with a hint) — expression mode still allows them.

- [nice-to-have] brief text corrections: Beyond the items above, small inaccuracies: evalidate also rejects Is/IsNot, Tuple, Slice, FloorDiv, Pow (chained comparisons like `1 < q_a < 5` and the `None` constant are fine); `AnswerOption.value` is `.strip()`ped on save (spec.py:122-129) so compiled option literals must be trimmed; params are also NOT validated at run time (BaseInstruction.__init__ has the schema validation commented out, instruction_engine/base.py:33-36) so the FE required-param save issue is the only guard; `authorize_update` is also invoked by `authorize_destroy`/`set_organizations` with the DRF request as `request_obj`, which is harmless.
    -> Fold these into the brief's 'Backend contract' section so the implementer does not re-derive them; trim option values in the value select.

Nothing at save time catches `patient.age` (attribute access), list literals, `is None`, tuples — all rejected by evalidate only at submit (verified).
    -> Extend the soft warning to referenced questions that carry `enable_when` or sit under a group with `enable_when` ('If this question is hidden or left unanswered, the submission fails'). In expression mode add a cheap lint from the existing tokenizer: flag `other` tokens (a `.` outside a number = attribute access, `is`, `[`/`(` followed by a literal = list/tuple literal) as a save issue `action_issue_expression_unsupported`. Builder must type literals from the target shape (unquoted numbers for integer/decimal/quantity/`patient.age`).

- [should-change] fill-side outcome scope (brief 'Fill-side outcomes'): Only `logging` (NOTIFY, echoes its params — base.py:43-49, logging_test.py:22-26) exists; REDIRECT/VALIDATE/TEXT/PERFORMED handling and same-origin redirect navigation have no consumer, which conflicts with the owner's 'no extension points without a second consumer' constraint. `instruction_type` arrives as the enum's string value.
    -> Implement NOTIFY only: if `results.message` is a string, `toast.info(message)`; for any other entry `toast.info(t('action_ran', {slug}))`. Drop the REDIRECT navigation path and the `onSuccess(redirect?)` signature change until a REDIRECT instruction ships.

- [nice-to-have] date/time/url operators (brief line 128): Cleaned values are exactly the strings the FE serialises: date `yyyy-MM-dd` (serializeValues.ts:27-33), time `HH:mm:ss` (:37-46), dateTime ISO with offset (:34-36), url verbatim (probe). Equality on dateTime is practically unusable (offset formatting varies) and string comparison operators are not offered anyway.
    -> Offer `is`/`is not` with a date input for `date` only; hide `time`, `dateTime` and `url` from the builder picker (mark `unusable: "type"` with a hint) — expression mode still allows them.

- [nice-to-have] brief text corrections: Beyond the items above, small inaccuracies: evalidate also rejects Is/IsNot, Tuple, Slice, FloorDiv, Pow (chained comparisons like `1 < q_a < 5` and the `None` constant are fine); `AnswerOption.value` is `.strip()`ped on save (spec.py:122-129) so compiled option literals must be trimmed; params are also NOT validated at run time (BaseInstruction.__init__ has the schema validation commented out, instruction_engine/base.py:33-36) so the FE required-param save issue is the only guard; `authorize_update` is also invoked by `authorize_destroy`/`set_organizations` with the DRF request as `request_obj`, which is harmless.
    -> Fold these into the brief's 'Backend contract' section so the implementer does not re-derive them; trim option values in the value select.

section='''## Actions (submit-time automations)

A questionnaire carries `actions` — rules the backend evaluates when a
patient/encounter questionnaire is submitted (`POST …/submit/`): each is a
`condition` (a Python-subset expression run by `evalidate`) over the cleaned
answers (`q_<link_id>`) and registry context values (`patient["age"]`),
plus `instructions` (`{slug, params, context}`) executed when it holds.
Resource-subject questionnaires (location/device/facility) never run them.

- Types and routes: `src/types/questionnaire/actions.ts`,
  `actionApi.ts` (`action_configuration/instructions|fields`), keys in
  `queryKeys.ts` (`actionRegistryKeys`). `normalizeQuestionnaireActions`
  is the wire-shape guard every read goes through.
- `shared/actionExpression.ts` — the one bridge between the editor and the
  stored strings: `compileCondition`/`parseCondition` for the canonical
  rule subset (`ref OP literal` joined by one connective; anything else is
  a "custom expression" edited as text), message templates
  (`{answer}` tokens ↔ `{{ f"…" }}`), `lintExpression`, reference
  extraction and the clone remap. Node-tested; keep it free of component
  imports.
- `builder/actionVariables.ts` — what a rule may reference and how each
  answer compares (see the value-shape notes in the file: quantities are
  `{value,…}` records, valueset choices compare by `coding.code`,
  repeating-group children are not top-level names).
  `builder/actionValidation.ts` — the save rules; `builder/actions/` — the
  editors the inspector composes.
- `studio/ActionsPanel.tsx` — the inspector target the outline's Actions
  row selects; `studio/useActionRegistry.ts` fetches the registry.
- Fill side: `fill/submit/validateActionReferences.ts` blocks a submission
  whose action references a visible unanswered question (the backend would
  500 and roll the batch back); `fill/submit/actionOutcomes.ts` reads
  `_actions` off the submit results and `FillPageBody` toasts them after
  the redirect.

Backend gaps the UI works around (ENG-737 as of 2026-09-03): an unanswered
`q_` reference raises at submit (500, whole batch rolled back); condition
syntax and instruction params are not validated at save time; the registry
lists fields twice; the only registered instruction is the `logging`
smoke test; `PatientQuestionnaire` registers no context fields; the
questionnaire create/update hooks require `actions` to be present (the FE
always sends it, `[]` at minimum).

'''
s=s.replace(marker, section+marker)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("readme ok")

setup("authenticate", async ({ page }) => {
  // Navigate to login page
  await page.goto("/login");

  // Fill in credentials
  // These should match the credentials from your local backend setup
  await page.getByRole("textbox", { name: /username/i }).fill("admin");
  await page.getByLabel(/password/i).fill("admin");

  // Click login button
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: /login/i }).click();

  // Wait for successful login - adjust based on your app's behavior
  // This could be checking for a redirect, a user menu, etc.
  await page.waitForURL(/(?!.*login)/, { timeout: 15000 });

  // Verify we're logged in by checking for user-specific elements
  // Adjust this selector based on your application
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: /^Hey .+/ })).toBeVisible();

  // Save signed-in state to 'authFile'
  await page.context().storageState({ path: authFile });
});

---
name: project-questionnaire-actions
description: Questionnaire actions UX (studio Actions panel + fill-side outcomes) built 2026-09-03 on bodhi/questionnaire-actions against backend ENG-737; contract facts, env gotchas, and open backend gaps
metadata:
  type: project
---

Built 2026-09-03 (uncommitted on `bodhi/questionnaire-actions` at session end): the
questionnaire **actions** UX against care backend ENG-737. Studio: outline row "Actions"
→ inspector `studio/ActionsPanel.tsx` (collapsible cards, When = rule builder over
`shared/actionExpression.ts` with expression escape hatch, Then = registry-driven
instruction editors, `{answer}` message tokens compiled to `{{ f"…" }}`); fill:
`fill/submit/validateActionReferences.ts` guard + `_actions` toasts after redirect.
Specs: `tests/facility/settings/questionnaires/questionnaireActions.spec.ts`,
`tests/facility/patient/encounter/fill/fillActions.spec.ts`. README has an Actions section.

**Backend contract facts (verified by probes):** `actions[] = {condition, instructions[{slug,
params, context}]}`; evaluated only on patient/encounter `submit/`; `evalidate` whitelist has
NO Attribute (`patient["age"]` not `patient.age`), NO list literals; answers are `q_<link_id>`
present ONLY when answered (unanswered ref → 500 + batch rollback); cleaned shapes: boolean
True/False, quantity `{value,unit,coding}` (compare `q_x["value"]`), valueset choice
`{coding}` only (compare `q_x["coding"]["code"]`), option choice = bare string even with
codes, repeats = list, repeating-group children are NOT top-level names; `{{ … }}` params
are whole-value templates (untrimmed check); `_actions` is `{}`/`[]`/list on the submit
response and rides `results[i].data` through the batch endpoint. Only instruction is
`logging` (NOTIFY, echoes `{message}`). Registry fields come back duplicated.

**Why:** link ids default to `Q_xxxxxxxx` now (was `Q-…`, not a Python name); legacy
hyphenated ids are auto-renamed via reducer `renameLinkId` when picked in a condition.

**How to apply / gotchas:** `.env.local` points `REACT_CARE_API_URL` at develop-api — for
Playwright build AND run with `REACT_CARE_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000` exported (the
spec helpers read it too). Snapshot the DB first (`POSTGRES_PORT=5433
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED ./scripts/playwright-db.sh snapshot`), run setup with
`--workers=1` (questionnaire.setup.ts fails on ENG-737 — expected), then specs with
`--no-deps PLAYWRIGHT_DB_SNAPSHOT=/nonexistent`. Open backend gaps to raise on ENG-737:
origin/ENG-737's create/update hooks iterate `actions` and 500 when the key is absent (the
local Docker checkout carries an UNCOMMITTED `_submitted_actions()` guard); no save-time
validation of condition syntax/params; unanswered-ref 500; PatientQuestionnaire registers
no fields. Related: [[project-questionnaire-v2]], [[feedback-minimal-abstraction]].

content.text:
The actions UX is built, verified end to end, and left uncommitted on `bodhi/questionnaire-actions` for your review.

**What you get**

- **Studio, Actions panel.** The outline has an "Actions" row under Form settings (count badge, warning icon, and a ⚡ cue on any question an action reads). The inspector shows one collapsible card per action with a plain-words summary ("Runs when “Fever” equals “Yes” → Show a message"). Files: [ActionsPanel.tsx](src/components/QuestionnaireV2/studio/ActionsPanel.tsx), [builder/actions/](src/components/QuestionnaireV2/builder/actions/).
- **When block.** Field / operator / value rows with AND/OR, mirroring the Logic tab. Operators and value controls follow the backend's cleaned answer shapes (booleans, numbers, option choices, multi-select "contains", valueset choices by code, quantities by value). "Edit as expression" is the escape hatch; anything the builder can't read opens as an expression with insert chips and a guarded way back.
- **Then block.** Instruction picker driven by the registry (plain names, never slugs), inputs generated from `input_schema`. Message inputs accept `{answer}` tokens inserted at the caret and compile to the backend's f-string template, with a preview line. "Applies to" is resolved automatically and only shown when it is not the submission itself.
- **Safety rails.** Save is blocked by action issues in the existing "N to fix" popover: empty condition, no steps, unknown instruction, missing required input, reference to a deleted question, attribute-access or syntax errors in expressions, and references to conditionally shown questions. Optional referenced questions get a warning with a one-click "Mark required".
- **Fill side.** A visible referenced question left blank is flagged on the field before submit, since the backend otherwise returns a 500 and rolls the whole batch back. Outcomes from `_actions` show as toasts after the redirect, titled by the instruction's name. A 5xx on the questionnaire's own request now says the form's actions failed rather than "validation failed".
- **Plumbing.** Generated link ids are now `Q_xxxxxxxx` (a hyphen can't be a Python name); picking a legacy `Q-…` question auto-renames it and follows the rename through enable_when and every action. Clone remaps action references. Create and update always send `actions` explicitly.

**Verification**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unit tests (`npm run test:unit`) | 160 pass |
| tsc, full ESLint | clean, 0 errors in new files |
| New Playwright specs (studio + 2 fill) | 3 pass |
| Regression specs (studio chrome, conditions, import/clone, enableWhen, builder, patient fill) | 14 pass |
| Browser check of the built studio | panel, condition row, instruction render as designed |

**Design decisions you may want to revisit**

- I kept the structured rule builder plus a parser for its own canonical subset rather than raw text with chips. The maintainability critique argued for raw text; I judged the builder to be the actual UX value for admins, and the module is pure and node-tested in [actionExpression.ts](src/components/QuestionnaireV2/shared/actionExpression.ts).
- Only the `{message}` outcome convention is handled. REDIRECT/VALIDATE branches were cut until an instruction produces them.

**Backend gaps to raise on ENG-737** (documented in the module README too)

- The pushed branch's create/update hooks iterate `actions` and crash when the key is absent. Your local Docker checkout has an uncommitted `_submitted_actions()` guard in the questionnaire viewset that hides this; it needs to land.
- An unanswered `q_` reference raises at submit and rolls the batch back. Condition syntax and params are not validated at save time. `PatientQuestionnaire` registers no context fields. The registry lists fields twice.

**Environment notes**

- `.env.local` points builds at develop-api. For Playwright, build and run with `REACT_CARE_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000` exported. The enable-when fixture setup still fails on ENG-737 as before.
- I took a Playwright DB snapshot of the current local state so restores work; the setup run refreshed the auth files.

Nothing is committed. Two follow-ups I left out: a Link ID editor in the inspector (legacy ids are handled by the auto-rename instead) and a valueset picker for coded-choice conditions (a code text input is used).

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from django.conf import settings
from django.template import TemplateDoesNotExist
from django.template.loader import render_to_string
from django.utils.module_loading import import_string

from care.utils.sms.message import TextMessage

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from care.utils.sms.backend.base import SmsBackendBase


def get_sms_content(template_path: str, context: dict) -> str:
    try:
        return render_to_string(template_path, context)
    except TemplateDoesNotExist:
        error = f"Template '{template_path}' not found."
        raise TemplateDoesNotExist(error) from error


def initialize_backend(
    backend_name: str | None = None, fail_silently: bool = False, **kwargs
) -> "SmsBackendBase":
    """
    Load and configure an SMS backend.

    Args:
        backend_name (Optional[str]): The dotted path to the backend class. If None, the default backend from settings is used.
        fail_silently (bool): Whether to handle exceptions quietly. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        SmsBackendBase: An initialized instance of the specified SMS backend.
    """
    backend_class = import_string(backend_name or settings.SMS_BACKEND)
    return backend_class(fail_silently=fail_silently, **kwargs)


def send_text_message(
    content: str = "",
    sender: str | None = None,
    recipients: str | list[str] | None = None,
    fail_silently: bool = False,
    backend_instance: type["SmsBackendBase"] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """
    Send a single SMS message to one or more recipients.

    Args:
        content (str): The message content to be sent. Defaults to an empty string.
        sender (Optional[str]): The sender's phone number. Defaults to None.
        recipients (Union[str, List[str], None]): A single recipient or a list of recipients. Defaults to None.
        fail_silently (bool): Whether to suppress exceptions during sending. Defaults to False.
        backend_instance (Optional[SmsBackendBase]): A pre-configured SMS backend instance. Defaults to None.

    Returns:
        int: The number of messages successfully sent.
    """
    if isinstance(recipients, str):
        recipients = [recipients]

content.thinking: The registries make adding fields/instructions cheap—right now only a basic `patient`→`age` field and a `logging` instruction exist, but I identified real backend support for several new fields (patient/encounter attributes) and instructions (notify, set priority, add note, tag, SMS). One caveat: the branch needs an uncommitted local fix carried over, so I'll lay out the options for how to proceed.

questions.question: Which instructions should the backend register?

options.label: Message + encounter priority (Recommended)
options.description: A real 'Show a message' NOTIFY instruction and 'Set encounter priority' (enum input). Smallest useful set, no external services.

options.label: Add a note on the encounter
options.description: Creates a note thread/message on the encounter with a templated text (answers spliced in).

options.label: Tag the patient or encounter
options.description: Applies a TagConfig to the patient or encounter via the existing tag manager; input is a tag picked from the facility's tags.

options.label: SMS the patient
options.description: Sends a text to the patient's phone via the SMS backend. Real sends in prod (SNS); I would gate it behind a setting.

questions.question: Should I also harden the evaluator in the same branch?

options.label: Full hardening (Recommended)
options.description: Commit the MISSING guard, seed unanswered q_ names as None so conditions never 500, and validate condition syntax + instruction params at save time.

options.label: Only commit the MISSING guard
options.description: Just the existing local fix; leave evaluator semantics to Vignesh.

questions.question: Where should the backend work go?

options.label: New stacked branch (Recommended)
options.description: bodhi/ENG-737-actions-catalog off your bodhi/ENG-737-test-fixtures, including the uncommitted guard, ready for a PR into ENG-737.

options.label: Directly on ENG-737
options.description: Commit onto Vignesh's branch and push.

Everything is verified; nothing further to request. Here is the wrap-up.

**Backend catalog** — committed on the new care branch `bodhi/ENG-737-actions-catalog` (stacked on your `bodhi/ENG-737-test-fixtures`, commit `6a568c5ae`, not pushed):

- **Fields.** `PatientQuestionnaire.patient` and `EncounterQuestionnaire.encounter` edges, a new `Encounter` context (status, encounter_class, priority), and Patient values: gender, name, phone_number, date_of_birth, year_of_birth, blood_group, deceased. Patient forms now have context fields too.
- **Instructions.** `show_message` (Notification), `set_encounter_priority` (enum input, permission-checked, no-op with a message if already set), `tag_encounter` and `tag_patient` (through the existing tag managers; a facility tag lands in the facility's set, an instance tag in the instance set). Save-time `authorize()` rejects unknown priorities, tags of the wrong resource, and tags the author may not apply.
- The tag params carry `x-care-picker: tag_config` / `x-care-resource` as `json_schema_extra` — the convention the studio uses to render a picker.
- 8 backend tests in `care/action_evaluator/tests/` pass (registry contents, message templating with patient fields, conditions on encounter/patient context, priority escalation and idempotence, tagging both resources once, and the three save-time rejections). Ruff clean.
- Per your choice, no evaluator changes. The `_submitted_actions()` guard is still an uncommitted edit in that checkout; without it, origin/ENG-737 still crashes on any create or update that omits `actions`.

**Frontend** (uncommitted, on top of yesterday's work):

- Enum params (`$ref` into `$defs`) render as a select with readable labels; `x-care-picker: tag_config` renders a tag picker scoped to the studio mount's facility ([TagConfigParamPicker.tsx](src/components/QuestionnaireV2/builder/actions/TagConfigParamPicker.tsx)).
- Plain names for the new instructions; `logging` is now labelled "Log a message (test)".
- Verified live in the studio: "Tag the patient" lists the facility's three patient tags and shows "Applies to: Patient"; "Set encounter priority" shows the 13 priorities and "Applies to: Encounter"; filling the tag clears the "required input" save issue.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Backend tests (`care.action_evaluator`) | 8 pass |
| Frontend unit tests | 160 pass |
| tsc, ESLint (changed files) | clean |
| Playwright: actions specs (studio + 2 fill), conditions authoring | 9 pass |

**Two things worth knowing**

- The studio spec had to dismiss the app's "Software Update" toast: it appears top-centre on a reload under the preview server and sits over the top bar's "N to fix" button. Real users can close it, but a persistent top-centre toast covering the header is a pre-existing UX hazard beyond this work.
- For Playwright here, both the build and the test process need `REACT_CARE_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000` exported, since `.env.local` points at develop-api.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(questionnaire-v2): questionnaire actions — studio authoring and fill-time outcomes

Backend ENG-737 adds `actions` to questionnaires: submit-time rules (a Python-subset
condition over the answers and context values, plus registry instructions). This is the
UX for them.

Studio: an "Actions" row under Form settings opens an inspector panel of collapsible
action cards. "When" is a rule builder (field / operator / value, AND/OR) over the
canonical expression subset in shared/actionExpression.ts, with a plain-text expression
escape hatch; "Then" is a registry-driven instruction list whose inputs come from each
instruction's input_schema (strings take `{answer}` tokens compiled to whole-value
f-string templates, enums render as selects, `x-care-picker: tag_config` renders a
facility-scoped tag picker). Save rules block references to deleted or conditionally
shown questions, unknown instructions, missing required inputs and expressions the
evaluator would reject; the top bar's issues popover lists them beside the question
rules. Generated link ids are now `Q_xxxxxxxx` (identifier-safe); picking a legacy `Q-…`
question renames it and follows the rename through enable_when and every action. Clone
remaps action references through the regenerated link ids.

Fill: a referenced question left blank is flagged on the form before submission (the
backend would otherwise 500 and roll the batch back); a 5xx on the questionnaire's own
request is reported as the form's automation failing; `_actions` outcomes from the
submit results are toasted after the redirect, titled by the instruction's name.

Tests: node suites for the expression module, variables graph, validation, reducer and
outcomes; Playwright for authoring (round trip, reload, issue gating, expression mode)
and fill (message toast, reference guard).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
